statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the number of neighbours found to satisfy rule A per representative, divided by the probability 2^-8 that a trial satisfies rule A, is at least 40.02 on the run as a whole, so that a representative yields at least 41.02 trial-equivalents on average over a run: one for itself and 40.02 for the neighbours its gate opens. H4 is a premise of the success probability of proof.md Section 7 and of the time bound of Section 8, which charges per trial-equivalent and divides the cost of a representative by 41.02.
scope: The clusters of proof.md Section 6.7 on the trials of Section 6.4: a representative is a trial whose bits 14, 30 and 31 of e1 = Y3 + Y4 and of X2 are zero; its 63 neighbours are the trials reached by flipping a non-empty subset of those six bits, and they are examined only when the representative passes the gate, the four conditions of rule A that bits 0, 16 and 17 of h1 are zero and bit 1 is one. The statement is about the average over the representatives of a run; it is not claimed outer step by outer step and is false for single outer tuples, whose yields run from 15.9 to 57.1.
extrapolation: From participant measurements on real messages of the sub-class, each with its own program and its own reference for the words of a trial: 40.018 +- 0.012 over 16,777,218 opened representatives, each on a fresh random outer tuple; 40.032 +- 0.075 and 40.056 +- 0.248 in two runs that enumerate all 16,384 representatives of a value of X2 in member order and then every trial of every cluster; 40.027 +- 0.010 by another AI model (Grok 4.7) with a program and a reference of its own; and 40.117 and 39.802 by a fourth agent over 4,096 and 128 outer steps. An opened cluster finds 2.5008 neighbours that satisfy rule A on average, and the gate opens for 0.0624630 of the representatives. All in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled outer tuples to the average over the outer steps of one run.
limitations: Not organizer-verified. The yield is a measured mean, not a count, and no bound for it exists. It depends on the outer tuple: the neighbours found per representative have a standard deviation of about 14 per cent between outer tuples, and single tuples run from 15.9 to 57.1 in yield (13.7 and 13.2 per cent, and 16.07 to 54.90, in the fourth agent's runs). Every run that measured it used random outer words rather than the walk of Section 6.4; that the average over the outer steps of one run, which share four seed words, is at least 40.02 is assumed. The six flips and the gate were chosen by measurement on a sampler, by a screen of 231,525 flip sets and a beam search, which tends to find a set that happens to look good; the chosen set was remeasured on larger samples by three programs, and another AI model's re-screen checks the screen, not the run. The claimed time is proportional to 1 / (1 + 40.02): a yield lower by one part in ten raises it by about 0.15. No run of the cluster procedure end to end with the gate carried to the neighbours as at full size exists (proof.md Section 10).

statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the trials that the algorithm examines, the representatives and the neighbours of each representative whose gate opens, carry per trial at least the collision mass that rule A keeps on average over the whole sub-class, and the good trials of a run (R = 0 and rule A) do not come in clusters any more than H1 already allows; in particular the collisions of one cluster of 64 trials do not clump. H1 is read over the examined trials under this premise. H5 is a premise of the success probability of proof.md Section 7 and of the time bound of Section 8.
scope: The trials examined by the cluster procedure of proof.md Sections 6.4 and 6.7 in one run, compared with the trials of the sub-class that satisfy rule A. The first part is about the collision mass of one examined trial, the second about the event that two trials of one cluster are both good. Trials of one cluster share their six outer words and differ in three bits of X2 and three bits of e1.
extrapolation: First part: against the exact law of h1 in the sub-class, a decision diagram of 683,179 nodes from another AI model read by a helper agent with a reader of its own, the expected collision mass per examined trial divided by that per ordinary trial that satisfies rule A is 0.99950 +- 0.00036 on 1,325,033,143 clusters; a second agent measures 0.99994 +- 0.00006 on 1,032,096,571 examined trials; on a graphics card over 2^44.907 trials the first side over the 67 listed cells of beta and tau gives 1.0017 +- 0.0030, and 1.0000 on the four heaviest values of beta; GPT Sol 6.1 computed the factor exactly on three partial averages it could enumerate: 1.007971, 0.997446 and 1.000304. Second part: at the levels these tools reach the members of a cluster clump slightly negatively: a neighbour of a trial that satisfies rule A and carries one of the four heaviest values of beta carries one of them 0.9699 +- 0.0009 times as often as an independent trial, and Grok 4.7 measures the word of Lemma N zero on a neighbour, given zero on the representative, at 0.946 of the marginal rate at eight bits of agreement. All in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these proxies, at 2^-9, 2^-19 and about 2^-32, to the collision at about 2^-100.53.
limitations: Not organizer-verified. No measurement reaches the collision event. The first part is measured on proxies: its two sides must not be multiplied as independent factors, the other model says the factor for the whole ensemble is unknown and that a high retention of rule A does not imply that it is one, and the seven neighbours that flip only bits of X2 give 0.930 +- 0.059 on the 67 cells. The second part cannot be measured at full size: the collision has probability about 2^-100.53 per trial and the deepest events reached are about 2^-32 and 2^-40, so treating the measured clumping as a guide is an extrapolation over about 100 bits of conditioning; at twelve bits of agreement Grok 4.7 has 1.28 on only 11 events. A factor of ten at the level of tau would have shown in the counts; a factor of two would not. If an opened cluster fired as one trial, the claimed exponent would rise by about 1.32, and by 1.81 for 3.5 trials, most of the 2.2 that the clusters gain. Neither a reduced-word run end to end whose gate is carried to the neighbours at 0.6 to 0.87 as at full size, nor a proof that each of the six flipped bits still moves the collision given a collision at the representative, exists; the two scaled-down runs that exist carry the gate hardly (co-pass at most 0.41 against 0.25 by chance) and do not test this.

statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than G representatives of a run open their gate, fewer than W neighbour words of a run go through stage A and fewer than S neighbour words of a run enter stage 2, where G, W and S are the budgets of the neighbour path in step 4 of proof.md Section 6.4, each 1.2 times its measured mean per representative; so no budget of the neighbour path is reached.
scope: The gate of proof.md Section 6.7 (bits 0, 16 and 17 of h1 zero and bit 1 one, four of the eight conditions of rule A) on the representatives of Section 6.4, the nine neighbour words that an opened gate sends through stage A, and those of them in which a trial satisfies rule A, which enter stage 2. The budgets are G = 1.2 * 0.0624630 * 2,048 * J, W = 1.2 * 0.5625 * 2,048 * J and S = 1.2 * 0.1364 * 2,048 * J, each rounded down, with J as defined in step 4 of Section 6.4 (the constant RUN_PAIRS of the submitted program); 2,048 * J is the number of representatives in J pairs of an outer step and a value of X2, one for each cluster of 64 trials. Section 8 charges the neighbour path at 1.2 times the measured means, and the algorithm halts with failure when one of the three budgets is reached. The statement is about the totals over a run; it is not claimed value of X2 by value of X2 and is false for single values of X2.
extrapolation: From participant measurements on real messages of the sub-class over 256 random outer tuples with 32 random values of X2 each, every representative packed seven to a word in member order: the gate opens for 0.0624630 of the representatives, against 2^-4 = 0.0625 for a uniform h1; per representative 0.5625 neighbour words go through stage A (nine whenever the gate opens) and 0.1364 enter stage 2; three further programs reproduce each of these figures to within half a per cent (proof.md Section 10). The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled outer tuples and values of X2 to the average over the outer steps of one run.
limitations: Not organizer-verified. The budgets are 1.2 times measured means and are not proved. The count per value of X2 is not binomial: its variance is 11.18 times the binomial one pooled; single values of X2 have between 0.41 and 1.64 times the mean share of open gates, so single values of X2 exceed the budget, and the largest share seen for one value of X2 grows with the sample (1.64 times the mean over 8,192 values of X2, 1.72 over 16,384). Single outer tuples have between 0.058577 and 0.066032. That the average over the outer steps of one run, which share four seed words, stays below 1.2 times the measured means is assumed; the outer words of the samples are random words, not the walk of Section 6.4. If a budget were reached the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H6 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005.
